options.a: Lacked consideration or a legal purpose
options.b: Made only an oral agreement to buy land
options.c: Was induced by fraud or was a minor
options.d: Later found a better deal on another home

distractorExplanations.a: A contract missing consideration or a legal purpose is void or unenforceable, not voidable at one party's option.
distractorExplanations.b: An oral land contract is unenforceable under the statute of frauds, which differs from being voidable.
distractorExplanations.d: Buyer's remorse is not a legal ground; a valid contract cannot be avoided because a better deal appears.

wa-real-estate-readiness-check-agency-la.explanation: Fraud or lack of capacity can make a contract voidable by the protected party. Whether the contract is voidable depends on the circumstances.

options.a: A zoning variance that permits a nonconforming use of the lot
options.b: A claim, encumbrance, or defect that may impair marketability
options.c: The legal action used to clear disputed claims from a title
options.d: Constructive notice given by recording a deed in public records

distractorExplanations.a: Confuses land-use regulation with title; a variance is a zoning permission, not a claim against ownership.
distractorExplanations.c: That describes a quiet title action, which removes a cloud rather than being the cloud itself.
distractorExplanations.d: Recording gives constructive notice that protects title; it is not a defect impairing marketability.

options.a: Lets the lender demand full payoff if the property is sold
options.b: Requires extra payment if the borrower pays off early
options.c: Lets the lender accelerate the full balance after a borrower default
options.d: Charges a fee when the borrower's monthly payment arrives late

distractorExplanations.a: That is a due-on-sale (alienation) clause, which is triggered by a transfer rather than an early payoff.
distractorExplanations.c: That is an acceleration clause, which is triggered by default rather than by voluntary early payoff.
distractorExplanations.d: That is a late-payment charge; a prepayment penalty applies when the borrower pays early, not late.

wa-real-estate-readiness-check-finance-a.explanation: Prepayment penalties charge for early payoff when permitted by the loan terms and law. The penalty applies only when the note and law allow it.

options.a: Disclosure of the APR and finance charges to consumer borrowers
options.b: Lending discrimination based on race, sex, or marital status
options.c: Fees for referring settlement services in residential loans
options.d: Maximum interest rates that may be charged on certain loans

distractorExplanations.a: Credit cost disclosure is the Truth in Lending Act; usury laws cap the rate itself.
distractorExplanations.b: Credit discrimination is governed by the Equal Credit Opportunity Act, not usury laws.
distractorExplanations.c: Referral fees and kickbacks for settlement services are restricted by RESPA, not usury laws.

options.a: Conventional LTV is high (commonly above 80%)
options.b: An FHA loan is used with a down payment of 3.5%
options.c: A VA loan is used with no down payment at all
options.d: Conventional LTV falls to 78% of original value

distractorExplanations.b: FHA loans carry the government's mortgage insurance premium (MIP), not private mortgage insurance.
distractorExplanations.c: VA loans are guaranteed by the VA and do not require PMI even with no down payment; a funding fee applies instead.
distractorExplanations.d: 78% of original value is when borrower-paid PMI terminates under the Homeowners Protection Act, not when it starts.

options.a: Finance a short-term gap, often between purchase of a new home and sale of an existing one
options.b: Finance construction draws as a new home is built, then convert to a permanent loan
options.c: Combine a first and second mortgage to avoid PMI on an 80/10/10 purchase
options.d: Let a buyer take over the seller's existing loan on its original terms

distractorExplanations.b: That describes a construction (construction-to-permanent) loan, which funds building rather than a sale gap.
distractorExplanations.c: That describes a piggyback loan structure used to avoid PMI, not short-term gap financing between homes.
distractorExplanations.d: That describes a loan assumption, where the buyer takes over the seller's mortgage, not a bridge loan.

options.a: The seller's reason for selling and lowest acceptable price, even if the seller objects
options.b: Known latent defects or conditions that could significantly affect value or desirability
options.c: The racial or religious makeup of the neighborhood, since it may affect desirability
options.d: Obvious patent defects, while hidden latent defects are left for the buyer's own inspection

distractorExplanations.a: Seller motivation and bottom-line price are confidential client information, not material property facts a buyer must be told.
distractorExplanations.c: Commenting on a neighborhood's race or religion is steering under the Fair Housing Act, not a required material-fact disclosure.
distractorExplanations.d: Reverses the rule: known latent (hidden) defects are exactly what must be disclosed, because a buyer cannot readily discover them.

wa-real-estate-readiness-check-agency-la.explanation: Material property defects and legally required disclosures must be shared, as required by law; confidential motivations may be protected.

options.a: Public use and the owner's consent
options.b: Payment of the property's assessed value
options.c: A police-power finding without compensation
options.d: Public use/purpose and just compensation

distractorExplanations.a: Eminent domain is a forced taking; the owner's consent is not required, which is what distinguishes condemnation from a voluntary sale.
distractorExplanations.b: Just compensation is based on fair market value, not the tax assessor's assessed value, which is often lower.
distractorExplanations.c: Confuses eminent domain with police power: zoning and code regulation need no compensation, but a taking does.

wa-real-estate-readiness-check-property-.explanation: Takings require public use/purpose and just compensation under the Fifth Amendment (constitutional framework).

options.a: Obtain the highest price by carrying out every seller instruction, lawful or not
options.b: Owe the buyer customer the same loyalty and confidentiality as the seller
options.c: Guarantee the seller a closed sale at list price within the listing term
options.d: Promote the seller's interests with loyalty, care, and obedience within the law

distractorExplanations.a: Obedience extends only to lawful instructions; a broker must refuse illegal directions such as discriminatory or fraudulent ones.
distractorExplanations.b: Confuses client and customer: a buyer customer is owed honesty and fair dealing, not the fiduciary loyalty owed to the seller client.
distractorExplanations.c: Fiduciary duties concern conduct (loyalty, care, obedience), not guaranteed outcomes; brokers cannot promise a sale or price.

options.a: At closing, when the broker's compensation appears on the Closing Disclosure
options.b: Before or as soon as practicable when the dual/designated relationship arises
options.c: Only after an offer is accepted and both parties have signed the contract
options.d: After the inspection period ends, once the buyer is committed to the purchase

distractorExplanations.a: Closing is far too late; informed consent to dual or designated agency must come before the parties rely on it.
distractorExplanations.c: Waiting until after acceptance denies the parties informed consent during negotiations, when the conflict matters most.
distractorExplanations.d: Disclosure tied to a later contract milestone is too late; it is required when the dual relationship first arises.

wa-real-estate-readiness-check-agency-la.explanation: Agency disclosure timing is early—when the dual or designated relationship is created or contemplated, per applicable rules.

options.a: The listing broker earns a commission during the term except when the seller personally finds the buyer
options.b: Any cooperating broker who is the procuring cause earns the commission, and the seller may list with other firms
options.c: The listing broker is owed a commission if the property sells during the term, regardless of who finds the buyer
options.d: The broker keeps any proceeds above the seller's stated net price as compensation for the sale

distractorExplanations.a: That describes an exclusive agency listing, where the seller keeps the right to sell on their own without owing a commission.
distractorExplanations.b: That describes an open listing, where only the procuring broker is paid and the seller may list with several firms.
distractorExplanations.d: That describes a net listing, which is restricted or banned in many places; it is a compensation method, not exclusive right-to-sell.

wa-real-estate-readiness-check-agency-la.explanation: Exclusive right-to-sell typically protects the listing broker's commission if a sale occurs during the listing term (per the agreement).

options.a: Practicing law any time they fill in a standard form's blanks for a client
options.b: Permitted to draft custom clauses as long as the client signs a waiver
options.c: Practicing law if they draft novel legal clauses beyond authorized forms
options.d: Required to have the client's attorney approve each filled-in form first

distractorExplanations.a: Filling in approved standard forms is generally permitted for licensees; drafting new legal language is what crosses into law practice.
distractorExplanations.b: A client waiver does not authorize a licensee to practice law; drafting novel legal clauses remains unauthorized practice.
distractorExplanations.d: Attorney review may be advisable or a contract contingency, but it is not a general prerequisite to completing standard forms.

options.a: An obligation to purchase on stated terms within a period, once consideration is paid
options.b: A right of first refusal to match any offer the owner later accepts
options.c: An equitable title that passes legal title once payments are complete
options.d: A right to purchase on stated terms within a period, usually for consideration

distractorExplanations.a: Only the optionor (owner) is bound; the optionee holds a right, not an obligation, to buy, making the option unilateral.
distractorExplanations.b: A right of first refusal only lets the holder match a third-party offer; an option fixes the price and terms in advance.
distractorExplanations.c: That describes a vendee's position under a land contract (contract for deed), not an optionee's unexercised right.

options.a: Land bordering flowing water such as a river or stream
options.b: Land bordering a still lake, sea, or ocean
options.c: Water use based on first in time, first in right by permit
options.d: Ownership of subsurface minerals beneath a parcel of land

distractorExplanations.b: Confuses riparian with littoral rights, which apply to land bordering lakes, seas, and oceans rather than flowing water.
distractorExplanations.c: That describes the prior appropriation doctrine, a contrasting permit system, not riparian rights tied to bordering land.
distractorExplanations.d: Subsurface rights cover minerals and can be severed; riparian rights concern use of water by land bordering a stream.

options.a: Refuse to share any property facts until the buyer hires a buyer agent
options.b: Recommend an offer amount, since customers are owed the same advice as clients
options.c: Avoid acting as the buyer's advocate and stay within the listing agency role
options.d: Share the seller's lowest acceptable price so the buyer can make a fair offer

distractorExplanations.a: Listing agents owe customers honesty and may share property facts; the limit is on advocacy, not on providing information.
distractorExplanations.b: Confuses customer and client: advising a buyer on price is advocacy that conflicts with the agent's loyalty to the seller.
distractorExplanations.d: Revealing the seller's bottom line breaches the confidentiality the listing agent owes to the seller client.

wa-real-estate-readiness-check-agency-la.explanation: Listing agents represent the seller; advocacy for a buyer requires a proper agency shift and disclosure (or properly creating buyer agency if allowed).

options.a: Parties may still perform within a reasonable time after each stated deadline passes
options.b: The closing date is firm, but other contingency deadlines may slip
options.c: Contract dates and times are critical and late performance may be a breach
options.d: The offer expires if the seller does not accept it within 24 hours

distractorExplanations.a: That is the default rule when the clause is absent; time is of the essence makes the stated deadlines strictly enforceable.
distractorExplanations.b: The clause applies to all contract dates, including inspection, financing, and appraisal contingency deadlines.
distractorExplanations.d: Confuses the clause with an offer's expiration term; time is of the essence governs performance deadlines in the contract.

options.a: Use allowed in a district only after a special permit is issued
options.b: Lawful use that predates current zoning and may continue as is
options.c: Permission to deviate from a zoning requirement due to hardship
options.d: Permanent change of the zoning map for an entire district

distractorExplanations.a: That describes a conditional or special use permit, which allows a listed use under conditions rather than relief for hardship.
distractorExplanations.b: That describes a nonconforming use (grandfathered use), which predates the ordinance rather than being granted relief from it.
distractorExplanations.d: That is rezoning/amendment.

wa-real-estate-readiness-check-property-.explanation: Variances grant relief from strict zoning application in hardship cases, granted by the zoning authority (such as a board of zoning appeals).

options.a: The broker's compensation is the amount above a seller's net price
options.b: The broker's compensation is a fixed percentage of the final sale price
options.c: The seller keeps the right to sell on their own without owing a commission
options.d: The broker's flat fee is owed up front even if the property does not sell

distractorExplanations.b: That describes a standard percentage commission listing, which does not create the net listing's incentive to underprice.
distractorExplanations.c: That describes an exclusive agency listing, not a net listing where the broker keeps everything above the seller's net.
distractorExplanations.d: Confuses a net listing with a flat-fee or advance-fee arrangement; a net listing pays the broker only the excess over the net price.

wa-real-estate-readiness-check-agency-la.explanation: Net listings pay the broker the amount above the seller's net price, creating conflict-of-interest concerns: they can incentivize underpricing and are banned or tightly regulated in many places.

options.a: Exaggerated opinion that a reasonable person would not treat as a factual warranty
options.b: A seller's written warranty that the home's systems will stay defect-free after closing
options.c: Negligent misrepresentation of a material fact that the licensee should have verified
options.d: A credit-terms claim regulated under the Truth in Lending Act advertising rules

distractorExplanations.b: A written promise about condition is an express warranty that can be enforced, the opposite of non-binding opinion puffing.
distractorExplanations.c: A misstated measurable fact (size, age, room count) is misrepresentation, which creates liability; puffing is limited to opinion.
distractorExplanations.d: TILA/Regulation Z governs advertised financing terms such as APR and payments, not subjective sales opinions like "stunning views".

options.a: Proceed with the dual agency and obtain the seller's signed consent at or after closing
options.b: Represent both parties anyway but withhold the seller's confidential pricing information
options.c: Not create the dual agency relationship; consider designated agency, referral, or withdrawal
options.d: Proceed as a dual agent if the buyer consents in writing, since one party's consent is enough

distractorExplanations.a: Consent must be informed and given before dual agency begins; collecting it at closing makes it an undisclosed dual agency.
distractorExplanations.b: Keeping confidences does not cure the problem; acting for both sides without the seller's consent is still undisclosed dual agency.
distractorExplanations.d: Dual agency needs informed written consent from both clients; the buyer's consent alone cannot override the seller's refusal.

options.a: Using client trust money to pay brokerage expenses
options.b: Holding funds for several clients in one trust account
options.c: Disbursing funds per a written release agreement
options.d: Mixing client trust money with personal or operating funds

distractorExplanations.a: Spending trust money on the firm's own bills is conversion, a separate and more serious violation than mixing the funds.
distractorExplanations.b: A single pooled trust account for many clients is permitted when each client has its own ledger; it is not commingling.
distractorExplanations.c: Proper disbursement is compliance.

options.a: Survivorship
options.b: Devise by will
options.c: Homestead
options.d: Curtesy

distractorExplanations.b: A joint tenant cannot pass the interest by will; on death it passes to the surviving joint tenants, which defeats any devise.
distractorExplanations.c: Homestead protects a residence from certain creditors and is a separate statutory right, not a feature of joint tenancy.
distractorExplanations.d: Curtesy is a husband's marital interest in a deceased wife's land, a marital-rights concept unrelated to joint tenancy.

options.a: When the life tenant sells the interest
options.b: After 99 years, like a long-term ground lease
options.c: Upon the death of the measuring life
options.d: Upon the death of the remainderman

distractorExplanations.a: A life tenant may convey the interest, but the buyer then holds an estate pur autre vie that still ends at the measuring life's death.
distractorExplanations.b: A fixed 99-year term describes a leasehold or ground lease; a life estate is measured by a human life, not a set number of years.
distractorExplanations.d: The remainderman holds the future interest; his death does not end the life estate, which is measured by the life tenant or named life.

options.a: Hold title as one marital unit, so creditors of one spouse cannot reach it
options.b: Must hold equal shares acquired by the same deed at the same time
options.c: May hold unequal shares and typically lack survivorship unless specified
options.d: Cannot sell their share without consent of the other co-tenants

distractorExplanations.a: That describes tenancy by the entirety, a marital form; tenants in common need not be married and hold separate shares.
distractorExplanations.b: Equal shares from one deed at one time are the unities of joint tenancy; tenants in common may hold unequal, separately acquired shares.
distractorExplanations.d: A tenant in common may sell, mortgage, or will their share freely; co-tenant consent is not required.

options.a: Sending a copy to the county tax assessor's office
options.b: Recording the deed in the public land records
options.c: Having the deed notarized by a licensed notary
options.d: Delivering the signed deed to the grantee

distractorExplanations.a: The assessor's office keeps tax rolls, not the public land records; constructive notice comes from recording with the recorder/register of deeds.
distractorExplanations.c: Acknowledgment before a notary makes a deed eligible for recording; it does not itself give constructive notice.
distractorExplanations.d: Delivery and acceptance transfer title between the parties, but they give no notice to the world until the deed is recorded.

options.a: 0.25% of the loan amount
options.b: 1% of the purchase price
options.c: 1% of the loan amount
options.d: 10% of the down payment

distractorExplanations.a: 0.25% is a common estimate of how much one point lowers the interest rate, not what the point costs.
distractorExplanations.b: Points are based on the loan amount; with a down payment, 1% of the price overstates the cost of a point.
distractorExplanations.d: Wrong base.

options.a: Both interest and principal so the balance declines over the term
options.b: Interest only, with the full principal due as a balloon at maturity
options.c: Mostly principal early on, with the interest share rising over the term
options.d: Interest and principal, with the balance rising as unpaid interest accrues

distractorExplanations.b: That describes an interest-only or straight (term) loan with a balloon; an amortizing payment repays principal each month.
distractorExplanations.c: This reverses amortization: early payments are mostly interest, and the principal share grows as the balance falls.
distractorExplanations.d: A rising balance is negative amortization, which happens when payments do not cover interest; a fully amortizing loan balance falls.

options.a: Banning certain kickbacks and requiring settlement cost disclosures
options.b: Requiring disclosure of the APR and finance charge in credit ads
options.c: Prohibiting lending discrimination based on race, sex, or age
options.d: Capping the commission brokers may charge on federally related loans

distractorExplanations.b: APR and finance-charge disclosure in advertising comes from the Truth in Lending Act (Regulation Z), not RESPA.
distractorExplanations.c: Credit discrimination is prohibited by the Equal Credit Opportunity Act; RESPA addresses settlement services and kickbacks.
distractorExplanations.d: RESPA does not set or cap commissions; it bans unearned fees and referral kickbacks between settlement service providers.

wa-real-estate-readiness-check-finance-a.explanation: RESPA addresses settlement services, kickbacks, and related disclosures (with TRID integration for many loans). It applies to federally related mortgage loans (covered transactions).

options.a: Adjusts to the current prime rate at each period with no caps
options.b: Adjusts with the margin, while the index stays fixed for the term
options.c: Can adjust only downward from the start rate, per federal rules
options.d: Can adjust based on an index plus margin, subject to caps

distractorExplanations.a: ARMs follow whatever index the note names and usually carry periodic and lifetime caps; uncapped prime tracking is not the rule.
distractorExplanations.b: This reverses the parts: the index moves with the market, while the margin is the fixed spread added to it.
distractorExplanations.c: Rates can rise or fall with the index within the caps; no federal rule limits ARM adjustments to decreases.

options.a: Physical damage to the structure from fire or storms
options.b: Lender losses when the borrower defaults on the loan
options.c: Title defects first created after the policy's effective date
options.d: Covered title defects and claims against ownership

distractorExplanations.a: Physical damage is a hazard or homeowner's insurance risk; title insurance covers ownership defects, not casualty.
distractorExplanations.b: Losses from borrower default are covered by mortgage insurance (PMI, FHA MIP), not by title insurance.
distractorExplanations.c: Title insurance covers defects existing as of the policy date; matters arising afterward are not covered.

options.a: The buyer is charged; it increases cash needed
options.b: The buyer receives a credit reducing cash to close
options.c: The item is prorated and split evenly between both parties
options.d: The seller is charged; it reduces the seller's proceeds

distractorExplanations.c: Proration divides an item by days of ownership and produces offsetting entries; it does not define what a buyer debit means.
distractorExplanations.d: A debit falls on the party in whose column it appears; a buyer debit charges the buyer, not the seller.
distractorExplanations.b: That describes a credit.

wa-real-estate-readiness-check-finance-a.explanation: Debits charge a party; buyer debits typically increase funds due at closing. A seller debit likewise reduces the seller's proceeds.

options.a: Set the federal funds rate that drives mortgage pricing
options.b: Buy and sell existing mortgages, improving liquidity for originators
options.c: Insure lenders against borrower default on high-LTV loans
options.d: Originate and fund new loans directly to borrowers at the closing table

distractorExplanations.a: The Federal Reserve sets the federal funds target rate; Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac buy loans but do not set that rate.
distractorExplanations.c: Default protection on high loan-to-value loans is the role of private mortgage insurance or FHA, not the secondary market.
distractorExplanations.d: Making and funding loans to borrowers is the primary mortgage market; the secondary market buys loans already made.

options.a: Criminal penalties with no license consequences
options.b: Review only at the next license renewal
options.c: A fine from the local MLS but no license action
options.d: License suspension/revocation proceedings

distractorExplanations.a: A conviction tied to practice is grounds for license discipline as well; the criminal case does not replace regulatory action.
distractorExplanations.b: The regulator can open a disciplinary case when it learns of the conviction; it does not wait for renewal.
distractorExplanations.c: An MLS is a private service that cannot discipline a license; license sanctions come from the state regulator.

wa-real-estate-readiness-check-wa-licens.explanation: Criminal convictions can trigger disciplinary cases. The case is brought by the Department of Licensing.

options.a: Regulated by HUD under the Fair Housing Act
options.b: Prohibited or restricted by advertising rules
options.c: Permitted when the ad lists the agent's phone
options.d: Allowed for agents selling their own property

distractorExplanations.a: HUD enforces discrimination rules in ads; disclosure of licensee and firm identity is a state license-law advertising rule.
distractorExplanations.c: A phone number alone does not tell consumers the ad is from a licensee or which firm placed it; the firm name is still required.
distractorExplanations.d: Licensees advertising their own property must still disclose licensed status; the blind-ad rule applies to them too.

options.a: May be required or strongly expected, but does not excuse license law violations
options.b: Covers intentional misrepresentation claims if the broker reports them promptly
options.c: Replaces the need for a seller disclosure statement on resale homes
options.d: Protects the buyer against title defects found after closing

distractorExplanations.b: E&O policies exclude intentional or fraudulent acts; prompt reporting does not bring fraud within coverage.
distractorExplanations.c: Insurance does not waive statutory disclosure duties; the seller disclosure statement is still required where the law demands it.
distractorExplanations.d: Title defects are covered by a title insurance policy; E&O covers the licensee's professional negligence claims.

options.a: Outside license law, since gifts are a contract matter
options.b: Banned under RESPA as kickbacks in every transaction
options.c: Subject to advertising and inducement rules
options.d: Allowed only if offered to buyers rather than sellers

distractorExplanations.a: Offering prizes to win listings is treated as advertising and inducement conduct under license law, not just a private contract term.
distractorExplanations.b: RESPA targets referral payments between settlement providers; a disclosed gift to a consumer is governed mainly by state rules.
distractorExplanations.d: Inducement rules apply to offers made to sellers and buyers alike; who receives the gift does not change the rules.

wa-real-estate-readiness-check-wa-licens.explanation: Inducements are regulated; deceptive or prohibited prizes can trigger discipline. They may be restricted or require clear disclosure of the terms.

options.a: Seller authorization per the listing agreement
options.b: The managing broker's approval, without the seller
options.c: Agreement from buyer agents who have shown the home
options.d: Notice to the MLS at least 24 hours in advance

distractorExplanations.b: List price is the seller's decision; a supervising broker cannot change it without the seller's authorization.
distractorExplanations.c: Buyer agents represent buyers and have no authority over the seller's listing terms, including the price.
distractorExplanations.d: MLS rules govern how a change is reported, not whether it is authorized; the seller must approve the price change.

wa-real-estate-readiness-check-wa-licens.explanation: Price is the seller's decision; agents need authority to change list price. The authorization is typically in writing, and brokerage policy may add steps.

options.a: Improper trademark/membership misuse and can also be deceptive advertising
options.b: Allowed for any active licensee, since REALTOR® is a generic job title
options.c: Permitted if the licensee belonged to the association at some earlier time
options.d: A matter for the MLS alone, with no effect on advertising compliance

distractorExplanations.b: REALTOR® is a registered membership mark of the National Association of REALTORS®, not a generic title for licensees.
distractorExplanations.c: The mark may be used only while membership is current; past membership does not allow continued use.
distractorExplanations.d: Misusing the mark misleads consumers about the licensee's status, so it can also violate state advertising rules.

options.a: Disclose the defect only to the buyer's inspector so the seller's form stays unchanged
options.b: Refuse to conceal legally required disclosures and consider withdrawal if the seller persists
options.c: Follow the instruction, since the seller completes the disclosure form, not the broker
options.d: Conceal it if the buyer signed an as-is clause and waived inspection

distractorExplanations.a: Telling the inspector does not meet the broker's own duty to disclose known material facts to the buyer.
distractorExplanations.c: The seller fills out the form, but the broker has an independent statutory duty to disclose known material defects.
distractorExplanations.d: An as-is clause and inspection waiver do not permit concealing known material defects; they limit repairs, not disclosure.

options.a: Acceptable if the seller is notified afterward
options.b: Permitted if the friend signs the showing log
options.c: A matter only for the MLS, not license law
options.d: Improper and a security/agency violation risk

distractorExplanations.a: Access requires the seller's authorization in advance; telling the seller after the entry does not make it proper.
distractorExplanations.b: Signing a log does not authorize an unlicensed, unaccompanied entry; lockbox access is limited to authorized licensees.
distractorExplanations.c: Unauthorized access breaches duties to the seller and can be license-law misconduct, not just an MLS rule issue.

options.a: A material misrepresentation that can trigger discipline and civil liability
options.b: Acceptable puffing if the figure is within 10% of the true size
options.c: The appraiser's responsibility, since appraisers measure the home
options.d: Cured by an MLS disclaimer telling buyers to verify all measurements independently

distractorExplanations.b: Square footage is a measurable fact, not opinion; knowingly overstating it by any margin is misrepresentation.
distractorExplanations.c: The listing licensee who publishes a figure they know is wrong is responsible for it, whatever the appraiser later finds.
distractorExplanations.d: A generic disclaimer does not excuse a knowing misstatement; it covers honest estimates, not figures the agent knows are false.

options.a: Be run by any licensed broker, without a managing broker license
options.b: Register only if more than five licensees work there
options.c: Be registered/comply with branch office rules when required
options.d: Use a separate trade name that is not registered to the firm

distractorExplanations.a: Washington requires a branch manager who holds a managing broker license; an ordinary broker license is not enough.
distractorExplanations.b: No headcount threshold applies; a branch office must be licensed whatever its number of licensees.
distractorExplanations.d: A branch must operate under the firm's licensed name(s); an unregistered trade name misleads consumers about the firm.

options.a: License discipline and civil claims
options.b: Contract rescission but no license action
options.c: MLS suspension but no license discipline
options.d: Liability for the seller but not the broker

distractorExplanations.b: Rescission is one civil remedy, but a licensee who hides a known defect also faces license discipline.
distractorExplanations.c: An MLS sanction is private; failing to disclose a known material defect is also a license-law violation.
distractorExplanations.d: A broker who knows of a material adverse condition has a separate duty to disclose it and shares the liability.

options.a: Amended by the listing broker
options.b: Followed as written by the parties
options.c: Revised by escrow if one party asks
options.d: Interpreted by the selling broker

distractorExplanations.a: The listing broker is not a party to the escrow instructions and cannot amend them alone.
distractorExplanations.c: Escrow acts on joint instructions; one party's request cannot change terms both parties signed.
distractorExplanations.d: Neither broker decides the meaning of escrow terms; escrow follows the written instructions of the parties.

wa-real-estate-readiness-check-wa-licens.explanation: Escrow agents/brokers follow written instructions and legal requirements. Brokers must not unilaterally rewrite disbursement terms; changes need the parties' signed agreement.

options.a: Which commission rate a broker must charge when offering a limited-service listing
options.b: How brokers must split fees with cooperating firms in MLS listings
options.c: What services a listing broker must still provide even in limited-service listings
options.d: Which disclosures a seller may waive when listing with a flat-fee broker

distractorExplanations.a: Commissions are negotiable and are not set by statute; minimum-service laws address duties, not prices.
distractorExplanations.b: Cooperative compensation is set by agreement and MLS policy, not by minimum-service or brokerage-service statutes.
distractorExplanations.d: Seller disclosure duties come from separate disclosure statutes and are not waived by choosing a flat-fee broker.
